Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

<!-- pr-standards:title -->
Hey! Your PR title `fix(#41232): add fish shell completion support` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

**Potential duplicate found:**

- **PR #41235**: `fix(cli): honor shell argument in completion command` - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/41235

This PR appears to be directly related to the current PR #41336. Both are addressing the same issue (#41232) and both involve adding/fixing shell completion support with multiple shell types (bash, zsh, fish). PR #41235 also adds shell argument handling to the completion command, which overlaps with the functionality in the current PR. You should check if #41235 is still open and whether it needs to be merged first or if this PR should be rebased on it.

This issue doesn't fully meet our [contributing guidelines](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**What needs to be fixed:**
- The **Description** field contains only an external link with no explanation of what the problem is. Please describe what happens: what CPU usage you observe, when it starts, and how long it lasts after hibernation resumes.
- **Steps to reproduce** is empty. Please provide steps to reproduce the issue (e.g., start OpenCode, hibernate the computer, resume, observe CPU usage).

Please edit this issue to address the above within **2 hours**, or it will be automatically closed.

---

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #31831: opencode process consumes high CPU constantly (similar high CPU symptom)
- #41066: orphaned serve process busy-loops at 100% CPU (similar busy-loop CPU spike)

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

Also affected on the desktop app (Windows). The attach button / file picker filters out .xlsx (and the attachment MIME sniffing rejects both .xls and .xlsx as binary), so spreadsheet files cannot be attached at all. Being able to drag-and-drop .xlsx and have it converted to Markdown tables (like the office-converter approach in the pending PRs) would be very useful. Looking forward to seeing this merged.

What version of Bun is running?

opencode：1.18.15
What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0X64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

After completely shutting down the computer using hibernation and then restarting it, I found that the 'bun' process was using excessively high CPU usage, exceeding normal levels.
What is the expected behavior?

After the computer restarts from hibernation, the CPU usage of bun is approximately 5%.
What do you see instead?

After restarting the computer from hibernation, the CPU usage of bun is approximately 65%.
Additional information

This issue occurred in OpenCode version 1.18.15.
It works normally after completely closing the process and restarting it.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #23287: Recovery of agentic workflow after system wakeup/sleep — same scenario of interrupted agent task needing automatic recovery
- #36349: V2: preserve subagent parent completion across restart — tracks the durable subagent relationship that gets lost on server restart
- #32713: Native background session autosaver / crash recovery mechanism — covers crash/abrupt-close recovery with session continuity

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #34776: Plugin-registered slash commands fail in Desktop app but work in CLI (same symptom — Desktop passes commands as raw text, CLI works correctly)
- #40823: Can't use any `/commands` on Desktop while CLI works fine (same Desktop vs CLI discrepancy with plugins installed)
- #37025: Slash commands broken in Desktop app (broader Desktop slash command regression)

If your issue is distinct from these (e.g. specific to v1.18.15 or the `magic-compact` plugin's command hook path), please add a note clarifying the difference.

+1 I see the same in Konsole too and seems to be opentui related ( [repro](https://github.com/ruinivist/repros/tree/opentui-bare-url-repro) ) example, full link is recognized in Konsole but not when rendered via opentui

Confirmed still present in v1.18.15 (reported via https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/41339). Verified end-to-end with a real plugin (magic-compact v1.2.2): same config works in CLI (command fires, backup session + summaries injected), Desktop passes \/magic-compact 5\ and \/magic-stats\ through as raw text. Plugin loads fine — it's the Desktop command dispatch path. Happy to test a fix build when available.
Duplicate of #34776 (and #40823, #37025) — same Desktop command dispatch regression. Confirmed reproduction details and the magic-compact case are posted on #34776. Closing to consolidate.

even when you use the shift key in the terminal, it now copies all the useless noise ascii rather than just the text you want;

_do not override normal user controls_
